_doc: attr-classification-overrides.json — the hand-authored, reseed-durable OVERRIDE layer for block_attributes classification corrections (role/derived_selector/css_property/css_element/css_state/css_tier/box_family/etc). Lifted verbatim from sgs-update-v2.py ATTR_CLASSIFICATION_OVERRIDES (Bean request, 2026-07-21). This is the single source of truth Bean asked for — sgs-update-v2.py now READS this file rather than declaring the dict inline. Applied AFTER the derived classifier layer (css-property-classifications.json) as Stage 1 sub-step C, so an override here wins on any field conflict with the derived layer. Records here exist to correct genuine mis-derivations OR to record cases where what the code DOES and what it MEANS differ (e.g. sgs/tabs tabIndicatorColour delivers via box-shadow but is a COLOUR value type) — never to correct plain accuracy bugs in the classifier, which should be fixed at the classifier itself. Two entries added 2026-07-21 for the value-type-vs-delivery-property fix: sgs/tabs tabIndicatorColour/tabActiveIndicatorColour resolve via the classifier chain-walk to box-shadow (render.php:84-100 colour_props array -> style.css:120 inset box-shadow underline) — accurate but unusable for a consumer picking a control type. The manifest (tabs/block.json supports.sgs.elements.tab.attrMap) already declares these as css:border-color (its own documented rationale: the active variant renders via [aria-selected='true'], not CSS :active, and drives the underline/box-shadow INDICATOR colour). css_property overridden here to border-color to match that already-established, coordinator-approved manifest vocabulary — a colour-family property a consumer control-picker can route to a colour picker, not a shadow control. 18 entries added 2026-07-22 (Spec 31 coupled UN-EXCLUDE + HOVER-LIFT): scaleHover (10 blocks, excl. sgs/post-grid whose scaleHover is a per-item css_element=card derived-selector attr with a multi-property css_property, out of this base-domain resolver channel) / grayscaleHover (4 blocks) / imageZoomHover (4 blocks incl. sgs/post-grid, whose imageZoomHover IS root-scoped) now carry css_property=transform|filter + css_state=hover — these attrs have NO un-suffixed base sibling (the effect only ever exists as a hover interaction), so the new converter.db.db_lookup.attr_for_state_property direct-lookup channel resolves them by (css_property, css_state) rather than the base+Hover-suffix-append convention tabIndicatorColour-style pairs use. 1 entry added 2026-08-02 (property_suffixes Rating/Speed suffix-role fix, migrations/2026-08-01-rating-speed-suffix-role.py): the property_suffixes 'Rating' suffix was reclassified from the wrong 'number-css-px' to the common case 'behaviour' (it is right for 3 of the 4 attrs it matches: sgs/star-rating.maxRating, sgs/google-reviews.minRating, sgs/testimonial.showRating are all configuration, not content). sgs/star-rating.rating is the one genuine exception — the star/numeric rating VALUE ITSELF, a content-bearing display value matching the existing 'rating' role's own exemplar (sgs/testimonial.ratingStars, registered by migrations/2026-06-21-register-rating-role.py). Declared here as a single-attr override rather than bending the suffix rule to fit the minority case, per this layer's job (Layer 3, applied LAST, wins over the suffix-derived role on any conflict) — see check_css_property_reseed.py's docstring for the layering contract.

fields._note: 2026-08-05 (Bean): role CORRECTED visual -> layout. `visual` was a copy-paste from the sibling tagBorderRadius (where visual IS right for border-radius); padding is spacing, which is what `layout` means per its roles.json entry. Bean asked for the hand role to be DROPPED so a mechanism would derive it -- tested empirically and it does NOT: decompose_attr_name proposes 'layout' in isolation, but with the role field removed and the row cleared, a full reseed left it NULL (attr_type='object', css_property NULL, so neither the main assignment nor the styling backstop claims it). Declared by hand with the CORRECT value rather than left unclassified. RETIREMENT CONDITION: remove when a reseed can assign 'layout' to this row unaided -- verify by clearing it and reseeding.

2026-08-05: sgs/responsive-logo now mirrors how every other SGS image block declares an image. `logoUrl` (attr_type='string') was added beside the existing `logoId` (number) — the sgs/media imageUrl+imageId shape, ID-wins-URL-fallback — so `alt` finally has a string sibling to name as its companion. walk.py:295 gates alt capture on `role == 'image-object' AND attr_type == 'string'`, which three bare attachment IDs could never satisfy; that is why `alt` was routed through the interim `authored-alt-text` category. RETIREMENT CONDITION MET: `authored-alt-text` existed for this one block and can now be retired. Note the LEDGER previously recorded the prefix->suffix RENAME as the retirement condition — that was wrong, and verified wrong post-rename: renaming changed no attr_type, so image-alt stayed non-viable. It is THIS change, the attr-shape mirror, that retires it.

2026-08-05 RESTORED after a REGRESSION. This role was briefly retired on the belief — taken from roles.json's own description — that 'icon-lucide' has NO consumer in the converter. That description is WRONG: the consumer is resolve_icon_kind() (converter/services/field_extractors.py:100-142) plus the ICON arm in converter/services/extraction.py:1100-1141, which dispatches on role.startswith('icon-'). Shipped at D263 (2026-07-03), live-verified on page 8. Retiring it routed the attr to 'identity' via the Tier-1 name regex and dropped it out of that dispatch, breaking test_icon_leaf_lifts_* in converter/tests/test_extraction.py (3 failed -> 6 passed on restore, proven by experiment). DO NOT retire this again without first running `pytest scripts/converter/tests/test_extraction.py -k icon` — `npm run build` does NOT cover converter/tests, so this regression ships green.

entries._why: Track B, 2026-08-04. The `price` slot lists "ribbon" among its own aliases, and load_slot_aliases() builds its map first-writer-wins over an unordered scan, so `price` claims the name before the dedicated `ribbon` slot (which exists) can register its own. A draft authoring a cta-section ribbon writes .sgs-cta-section__ribbon, which the price-derived selector cannot match. Measured: 10 such alias collisions exist, 4 touch a live sgs/% attr, 3 are wrong. Fixed by override, NOT by de-duplicating slots.aliases: 179 of 1170 attrs depend on that alias layer for genuine synonym work (title->heading, url->link, columns->column), so removing it would break ~175 rows to fix 3.

Track B, 2026-08-04. Same alias-collision class: the `text` slot claims "caption" as an alias, so sgs/media.caption seeded canonical_slot='text'. The block genuinely renders .sgs-media__caption (verified: 2 occurrences in its own source), which is what a draft would author.

Track B, 2026-08-04. Same alias-collision class, opposite remedy: the `card` slot claims "step" as an alias, so a number field's numeric increment (e.g. 0.01) seeded canonical_slot='card'. This attr is not a content slot at all, so the correct value is NULL rather than a better slot name — matching the sgs/product-card.priceNote precedent above. Corroborated independently by the Track A fingerprint, whose D1 detector vetoed this attr after examining every usage site.

fields._reason: css_property NULLed 2026-08-12. The derived layer (extract-signatures.py) reads hero/render.php, sees these three attrs composing ONE linear-gradient(), and gives ALL THREE css_property='background-image' on the same element/state/tier. That is a compound value split across N attrs, which the one-attr-per-slot routing model cannot express: db-consistency Check #1/#8 flag it as an ambiguous slot and the column-first resolver raises AmbiguousLayerAttrError at CLONE TIME. Every other block declaring the same gradient triple (container, cta-section, site-header, site-footer, trust-bar) already carries css_property=NULL here and clones fine — hero was the lone outlier, so this aligns it with the established norm rather than inventing a rule. Surfaced by the 2026-08-12 reseed re-deriving css_property (not caused by that session's edits; hero's gradients shipped at D579-D582). ⛔ Do NOT give ONE of the three the property back to 'break the tie' — a gradient needs all three, so routing a draft's background-image to any single one of them would be wrong in a different way.
